name: Detect vendor bank-detail fraud with Groq, Google DNS and n8n Data tables

parameters.formTitle: Vendor bank detail change - fraud check
parameters.formDescription: Paste the email that asks you to change a supplier payment account. Nothing gets paid until this check clears.

options.systemMessage:
You are a fraud analyst reviewing a supplier payment-change request for social-engineering pressure tactics ONLY. You cannot see the vendor register, so never comment on whether the bank details are correct.

Score pressure_score from 0 to 100, where 0 is a calm routine business message and 100 is heavy manipulation. List only the tactics you actually observe, drawn from: urgency, confidentiality, authority, threat, reassurance, isolation. If none are present, return an empty list and a low score. Keep the rationale to one sentence.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: { "pressure_score": 75, "tactics": ["urgency", "confidentiality"], "rationale": "The message asks for secrecy and speed, both classic social-engineering levers." }

parameters.completionTitle: ={{ $('Combine Into Final Verdict').item.json.risk_band }} - do not release this payment yet
PASS - no fraud indicators above threshold

parameters.content:
## Detect vendor bank-detail fraud (BEC guard)

### Who's it for

Bookkeepers and finance teams who pay supplier invoices and receive emails asking to change a vendor's bank account.

### What it does

Checks the request against suppliers you have already verified and returns BLOCK, REVIEW or PASS with the evidence behind it. A screening aid that decides whether to hold a payment. It does not replace calling the supplier back.

### How it works

The form takes the email as received. A data table supplies your verified vendor records. A Code node scores the deterministic signals: mod-97 checksum on IBANs, lookalike-domain distance with homoglyph folding, Reply-To against From, sender against your authorised contacts, and the account against the one on file. Non-IBAN formats such as US routing numbers are compared but not checksummed. Google DNS is queried for MX records. A Groq chat model rates pressure language only, capped at 20 of the 100 points, so text hidden in the email cannot change the verdict. Every check is written to an audit table.

### Requirements

Two n8n data tables and a chat model credential. No paid API.

### Setup

1. Create a data table Vendor Bank Register: vendor_name, vendor_domain, authorised_emails, known_iban, known_account_last4, verified_on, callback_phone.
2. Create a data table Payment Change Audit Log: checked_at, vendor_matched, from_address, claimed_iban, risk_band, risk_score, signal_codes, report.
3. Point both data table nodes at your tables.
4. Add your chat model credential on Groq Chat Model.
5. Tune the thresholds in Set Fraud Policy.

### Customization tips

Swap the form trigger for your mailbox trigger to check requests automatically. Add a notification node on the held branch.

## 1. Capture and policy

The form takes the email exactly as received. Every threshold lives in Set Fraud Policy rather than buried in expressions.

## 2. Deterministic checks

IBAN mod-97, lookalike-domain distance, Reply-To mismatch, unauthorised sender, account diff and an MX lookup. These carry 80 of the 100 points, before any AI runs.

## 3. Pressure language

The model rates social-engineering pressure only and never sees the register. Capped at 20 points, so injected text in the email cannot change the verdict.

## 4. Verdict and audit trail

BLOCK at 60, REVIEW at 30. Every check is logged either way. A held payment tells the approver to call the number already on file.
